content:
The Acid Rain Program, created under Title IV, used different approaches for sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector.

For sulfur dioxide, an allowance represented permission to emit one ton under an aggregate cap, with allowances traded among covered sources. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 units at 110 plants. Including substitution or compensating units, the Phase I total reached 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.

Nitrogen oxides followed a separate path. Regulation for certain coal-fired units began in 1996 and was rate-based, without a cap or allowance trading.

One program, two pollutants—and distinct mechanisms and timelines for each.
